   366→                except Exception as e:
   367→                    logger.error(f"Hypothesis evaluation failed: {e}")
   368→                    # Create checkpoint on error
   369→                    await self.thermal_manager._do_checkpoint(
   370→                        task_id=self.config.journey_id,
   371→                        phase=f"{domain.name}_error_{i}",
   372→                        progress={"error": str(e)},
   373→                        hypotheses_completed=self.total_hypotheses_evaluated,
   374→                        total_hypotheses=sum(len(d.hypotheses) for d in self.config.domains),
   375→                    )
   376→                    raise
   377→
   378→            mgr.end_session()
   379→
   380→        domain_duration = time.time() - domain_start
   381→
   382→        return {
   383→            "domain": domain.name,
   384→            "completed": hypotheses_completed == len(domain.hypotheses),
   385→            "hypotheses_completed": hypotheses_completed,
   386→            "hypotheses_total": len(domain.hypotheses),
   387→            "duration_hours": domain_duration / 3600,
   388→            "results": results,
   389→            "thermal_events_in_domain": len(
   390→                [e for e in self.thermal_events if e.get("domain") == domain.name]
   391→            ),
   392→        }
   393→
   394→    async def _evaluate_hypothesis_with_thermal(
   395→        self, hypothesis: str, mgr: CompoundSessionManager, domain: DomainConfig
   396→    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
   397→        """Evaluate a hypothesis with thermal monitoring."""
   398→        client = get_compound_client()
   399→
   400→        # Pre-execution thermal check
   401→        metrics = self.monitor.get_current_metrics()
   402→        logger.debug(
   403→            f"Pre-execution temps: GPU={metrics.gpu_temp_current}°C, "
   404→            f"CPU={metrics.cpu_temp_current}°C"
   405→        )
   406→
   407→        t0 = time.time()
   408→
   409→        # Execute with model
   410→        prompt = (
   411→            f"Research hypothesis: {hypothesis}\n\n"
   412→            f"Domain: {domain.name}\n"
   413→            f"Evaluate this hypothesis considering:\n"
   414→            f"1. Technical feasibility\n"
   415→            f"2. Alignment with FLUME architecture\n"
   416→            f"3. Potential impact on 8-hour journey\n\n"
   417→            f"Provide:\n"
   418→            f"- Coherence score (0.0 to 1.0)\n"
   419→            f"- Implementation approach\n"
   420→            f"- Expected outcomes"
   421→        )
   422→
   423→        response_text, _ = await client.generate(
   424→            prompt=prompt,
   425→            model="gemini-3-pro:local",
   426→            system=f"You are a {domain.skill_name} specialist evaluating research hypotheses.",
   427→        )
   428→
   429→        t1 = time.time()
   430→        duration = t1 - t0
   431→
   432→        # Post-execution thermal check
   433→        metrics = self.monitor.get_current_metrics()
   434→        logger.debug(
   435→            f"Post-execution temps: GPU={metrics.gpu_temp_current}°C, "
   436→            f"CPU={metrics.cpu_temp_current}°C"
   437→        )
   438→
   439→        # Parse coherence
   440→        coherence = self._parse_coherence(response_text)
   441→
   442→        # Speed metric
   443→        approx_tokens = len(response_text) / 4.0
   444→        tokens_per_sec = approx_tokens / duration if duration > 0 else 0.0
   445→
   446→        # Check speed threshold
   447→        if tokens_per_sec < self.config.min_speed_tokens_sec:
   448→            logger.warning(f"Speed {tokens_per_sec:.2f} tok/s below threshold")
   449→
   450→        return {
   451→            "hypothesis": hypothesis,
   452→            "response": response_text,
   453→            "coherence": coherence,
   454→            "tokens_per_sec": tokens_per_sec,
   455→            "duration_seconds": duration,
   456→            "domain": domain.name,
   457→            "skill_name": domain.skill_name,
   458→            "gpu_temp_c": metrics.gpu_temp_current,
   459→            "cpu_temp_c": metrics.cpu_temp_current,
   460→        }
   461→
   462→    def _parse_coherence(self, text: str) -> float:
   463→        """Parse coherence score from response text."""
   464→        coherence = 0.5  # Default
   465→
   466→        if "coherence score" in text.lower() or "0." in text or "1.0" in text:
   467→            try:
   468→                lines = text.split("\n")
   469→                for line in lines:
   470→                    match = re.search(r"0\.[0-9]+|1\.0", line)
   471→                    if match:
   472→                        coherence = float(match.group())
   473→                        break
   474→            except Exception as e:
   475→                logger.warning(f"Failed to parse coherence: {e}")
   476→
   477→        return max(0.0, min(1.0, coherence))  # Clamp to [0, 1]
   478→
   479→    async def _compile_results(self, domain_results: list[dict]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   480→        """Compile final results from all domains."""
   481→        total_duration = time.time() - self.start_time
   482→        total_hypotheses = sum(r["hypotheses_completed"] for r in domain_results)
   483→
   484→        # Get final thermal status
   485→        thermal_status = self.thermal_manager.get_status()
   486→        tdp_status = self.tdp_tracker.get_budget_status()
   487→
   488→        result = {
   489→            "journey_id": self.config.journey_id,
   490→            "completed": all(r["completed"] for r in domain_results),
   491→            "domains": domain_results,
   492→            "total_hypotheses_evaluated": total_hypotheses,
   493→            "domains_completed": sum(1 for r in domain_results if r["completed"]),
   494→            "duration_hours": total_duration / 3600,
   495→            "thermal_events": self.thermal_events,
   496→            "thermal_events_count": len(self.thermal_events),
   497→            "total_paused_minutes": thermal_status.get("total_paused_minutes", 0),
   498→            "final_temps": {
   499→                "gpu_c": thermal_status.get("gpu_temp_c", 0),
   500→                "cpu_c": thermal_status.get("cpu_temp_c", 0),
   501→            },
   502→            "tdp_consumed_wh": tdp_status.get("consumed_wh", 0),
   503→            "tdp_consumed_percent": tdp_status.get("consumed_percent", 0),
   504→            "ended_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
   505→        }
   506→
   507→        logger.info(f"=" * 80)
   508→        logger.info(f"8-HOUR JOURNEY COMPLETE")
   509→        logger.info(f"Duration: {result['duration_hours']:.2f} hours")
   510→        logger.info(f"Hypotheses: {result['total_hypotheses_evaluated']}")
   511→        logger.info(f"Thermal events: {result['thermal_events_count']}")
   512→        logger.info(f"TDP consumed: {result['tdp_consumed_percent']:.1f}%")
   513→        logger.info(
   514→            f"Final temps: GPU={result['final_temps']['gpu_c']}°C, "
   515→            f"CPU={result['final_temps']['cpu_c']}°C"
   516→        )
   517→        logger.info(f"=" * 80)
   518→
   519→        return result
   520→
   521→
   522→# Convenience function
   523→async def run_8hour_autoresearch_journey(
   524→    config: Optional[EightHourConfig] = None,
   525→) -> dict[str, Any]:
   526→    """Run a complete 8-hour autoresearch journey with thermal protection."""
   527→    executor = ThermalAutoresearchExecutor(config)

   529→

1→"""Autonomous research agent for training optimization.
     2→
     3→Elegant integration with Cohezion compound executor.
     4→Based on karpathy/autoresearch patterns.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import json
    10→import logging
    11→import subprocess
    12→import time
    13→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    14→from datetime import datetime
    15→from pathlib import Path
    16→from typing import Any
    17→
    18→from cohezion.compound.core.executor import CompoundExecutor, ExecutionConfig
    19→from cohezion.compound.models import ExecutionResult, Task
    20→from cohezion.reliability import get_circuit  # Issue #8
    21→from cohezion.research.config import ExperimentResult, ResearchConfig
    22→
    23→
    24→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    25→
    26→
    27→@dataclass
    28→class ResearchSession:
    29→    """Session state for research.
    30→
    31→    Minimal state tracking, delegates to Cohezion persistence.
    32→    """
    33→
    34→    session_id: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now().isoformat())
    35→    experiments_completed: int = 0
    36→    best_metric: float = float("inf")
    37→    best_checkpoint: Path | None = None
    38→    active: bool = True
    39→
    40→
    41→class ResearchAgent:
    42→    """Autonomous research agent.
    43→
    44→    Clean implementation (~200 lines) following elegant simplification.
    45→    Integrates with Cohezion's compound executor and metrics systems.
    46→
    47→    Inspired by karpathy/autoresearch but integrated into Cohezion ecosystem.
    48→    """
    49→
    50→    def __init__(
    51→        self,
    52→        config: ResearchConfig | None = None,
    53→        executor: CompoundExecutor | None = None,
    54→    ):
    55→        """Initialize research agent.
    56→
    57→        Args:
    58→            config: Research configuration
    59→            executor: CompoundExecutor for running experiments
    60→                     (creates new one if None)
    61→        """
    62→        self.config = config or ResearchConfig()
    63→        self.session = ResearchSession()
    64→
    65→        # Create executor if not provided
    66→        if executor is None:
    67→            executor = CompoundExecutor(
    68→                execute_fn=self._run_experiment_with_circuit_breaker,  # Issue #8
    69→                config=ExecutionConfig(max_retries=1),
    70→            )
    71→        self.executor = executor
    72→
    73→        # Circuit breaker for reliability (Issue #8)
    74→        self.circuit = get_circuit("research_agent", failure_threshold=5, recovery_timeout=60)
    75→
    76→        logger.info(f"ResearchAgent initialized: {self.session.session_id}")
    77→
    78→    def _run_experiment_with_circuit_breaker(
    79→        self,
    80→        task: Task,
    81→        context: dict[str, Any],
    82→    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
    83→        """Run experiment with circuit breaker protection (Issue #8)."""
    84→        # Check if circuit is open
    85→        if self.circuit.is_open():
    86→            logger.warning("Circuit breaker open, skipping experiment")
    87→            return "Circuit open", {"error": "Circuit breaker open", "skipped": True}
    88→
    89→        try:
    90→            result = self._run_experiment(task, context)
    91→            self.circuit.record_success()
    92→            return result
    93→        except Exception as e:
    94→            self.circuit.record_failure()
    95→            logger.error(f"Experiment failed, circuit breaker recorded: {e}")
    96→            raise
    97→
    98→    def _run_experiment(
    99→        self,
   100→        task: Task,
   101→        context: dict[str, Any],
   102→    ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
   103→        """Run single experiment.
   104→
   105→        This is the core execution function passed to CompoundExecutor.
   106→        """
   107→        experiment_id = task.id
   108→        start_time = time.time()
   109→
   110→        logger.info(f"Running experiment: {experiment_id}")
   111→
   112→        try:
   113→            # Run training with time budget
   114→            result = self._execute_training(
   115→                time_budget=self.config.experiment_time_budget,
   116→            )
   117→
   118→            # Parse result
   119→            metric_value = result.get("val_bpb", float("inf"))
   120→            duration = time.time() - start_time
   121→
   122→            # Check if improved
   123→            improved = metric_value < self.session.best_metric
   124→            if improved:
   125→                self.session.best_metric = metric_value
   126→                logger.info(f"New best metric: {metric_value:.4f}")
   127→
   128→            return (
   129→                f"Experiment {experiment_id}: {metric_value:.4f}",
   130→                {
   131→                    "coherence": metric_value,
   132→                    "duration_seconds": duration,
   133→                },
   134→            )
   135→
   136→        except Exception as e:
   137→            logger.error(f"Experiment {experiment_id} failed: {e}")
   138→            return (
   139→                f"Failed: {e}",
   140→                {
   141→                    "coherence": float("inf"),
   142→                    "duration_seconds": time.time() - start_time,
   143→                },
   144→            )
   145→
   146→    def _execute_training(self, time_budget: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
   147→        """Execute training with time limit.
   148→
   149→        Runs autoresearch-style training for fixed duration.
   150→        """

1→# Autoresearch: K-Search Autonomous Kernel Optimization
     2→
     3→Autonomous overnight experiment loop for the AMD E2E Model Speedrun competition.
     4→Synthesizes K-Search (tree-structured optimization) with popcorn-cli evaluation
     5→to systematically explore kernel parameter configurations on the MI355X runner.
     6→
     7→## Architecture
     8→
     9→```
    10→┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    11→│                  driver.py (main loop)               │
    12→│                                                      │
    13→│  ┌──────────┐  ┌────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐ │
    14→│  │ K-Search │→ │ Template   │→ │ popcorn-cli      │ │
    15→│  │ Tree     │  │ Generator  │  │ test → benchmark │ │
    16→│  │ SELECT   │  │            │  │ → leaderboard    │ │
    17→│  └────┬─────┘  └────────────┘  └────────┬─────────┘ │
    18→│       │                                  │           │
    19→│       └──── UPDATE/INSERT/PRUNE ←────────┘           │
    20→│             (results analysis)                       │
    21→│                                                      │
    22→│  Rate limiter: 1 leaderboard/hr/problem              │
    23→│  Budget: ~75 cycles/night (8 min/cycle)              │
    24→└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    25→```
    26→
    27→## Quick Start
    28→
    29→```bash
    30→cd research/challenges/luma_amd_speedrun/autoresearch
    31→
    32→# Dry run (no popcorn-cli needed, validates templates):
    33→uv run python driver.py --dry-run --max-cycles 5
    34→
    35→# Single kernel sprint:
    36→uv run python driver.py --kernel moe --max-cycles 20
    37→
    38→# Full overnight run (all 3 kernels, priority-weighted):
    39→uv run python driver.py
    40→
    41→# Limit cycles:
    42→uv run python driver.py --max-cycles 50
    43→```
    44→
    45→## File Structure
    46→
    47→```
    48→autoresearch/
    49→├── driver.py              # Main overnight experiment loop
    50→├── ksearch_tree.py        # K-Search tree (KNode, SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/PRUNE)
    51→├── generator.py           # Template-based submission.py generator
    52→├── evaluator.py           # Wraps popcorn-cli (test/benchmark/leaderboard)
    53→├── analyzer.py            # Result analysis → tree priority updates
    54→├── rate_limiter.py        # 1/hour/problem leaderboard gating
    55→├── templates/
    56→│   ├── gemm_template.py   # Parameterized GEMM ($KERNEL_TABLE, $DEFAULT_LOG2_KS)
    57→│   ├── moe_template.py    # Parameterized MoE ($KSPLIT_TABLE, $DEFAULT_KSPLIT)
    58→│   └── mla_template.py    # Parameterized MLA ($SPLITS_TABLE, $KV_FORMAT, $FAST_MODE)
    59→├── tree/
    60→│   ├── gemm_tree.json     # Pre-seeded K-Search tree (11 nodes)
    61→│   ├── moe_tree.json      # Pre-seeded K-Search tree (11 nodes)
    62→│   └── mla_tree.json      # Pre-seeded K-Search tree (14 nodes)
    63→└── results/
    64→    ├── gemm_runs.jsonl     # Experiment log (append-only)
    65→    ├── moe_runs.jsonl
    66→    └── mla_runs.jsonl
    67→```
    68→
    69→## How It Works
    70→
    71→### 1. K-Search Tree (`ksearch_tree.py`)
    72→
    73→Each kernel has a tree of "strategy" nodes. Each node encodes:
    74→- **strategy**: Human-readable description (e.g., "E=257,d=256,bs=16: sweep KSPLIT 1-6")
    75→- **parameters**: JSON dict for template substitution (e.g., `{"KSPLIT_TABLE": {...}}`)
    76→- **priority**: 0.0-1.0, used for selection (higher = more likely to be tried next)
    77→- **stagnation_count**: Incremented on non-improving attempts; pruned at K=7
    78→
    79→Operations:
    80→- **SELECT**: Pick highest-priority active leaf node
    81→- **UPDATE**: Record benchmark result, adjust priority, track stagnation
    82→- **PRUNE**: Auto-prune after 7 stagnant attempts (K=7 threshold)
    83→- **DECAY**: Periodically decay all priorities to encourage exploration
    84→
    85→### 2. Templates (`templates/`)
    86→
    87→Each template is a Python string with `$PARAM` substitution slots. The key innovation
    88→is **per-shape lookup tables**: instead of one KSPLIT for all shapes, each shape gets
    89→its own configuration.
    90→
    91→Template parameters:
    92→- **MoE**: `$KSPLIT_TABLE` (dict: "E_dexpert_bs" → KSPLIT value), `$DEFAULT_KSPLIT`
    93→- **GEMM**: `$KERNEL_TABLE` (dict: "M_N_K" → {kernel, log2_ks}), `$DEFAULT_KERNEL`
    94→- **MLA**: `$SPLITS_TABLE` (dict: "bs_kvseqlen" → num_splits), `$KV_FORMAT`, `$FAST_MODE`
    95→
    96→### 3. Evaluator (`evaluator.py`)
    97→
    98→Wraps `~/.local/bin/popcorn-cli submit`:
    99→- **test**: Correctness check (no rate limit)
   100→- **benchmark**: Per-shape timing + geomean (no rate limit)
   101→- **leaderboard**: Official score (1/hour/problem limit)
   102→
   103→Every variant runs test first; benchmark only on pass. Leaderboard only on new best.
   104→
   105→### 4. Driver Loop (`driver.py`)
   106→
   107→Each cycle (~8 minutes):
   108→1. **Select kernel** (priority-weighted: MoE 50%, GEMM 30%, MLA 20%)
   109→2. **SELECT** best node from kernel's K-Search tree
   110→3. **Generate** submission.py from template + node parameters
   111→4. **Test** via popcorn-cli (correctness check)
   112→5. **Benchmark** if test passes (get per-shape timings)
   113→6. **Analyze** results, update tree priorities
   114→7. **Log** to JSONL (crash-safe, append-only)
   115→8. **Leaderboard** submit if new best AND rate limit allows
   116→9. Sleep 5s, repeat
   117→
   118→### 5. Parameter Perturbation
   119→
   120→After a node's first attempt, the driver slightly perturbs parameters on subsequent
   121→attempts to explore the neighborhood:
   122→- MoE: Random KSPLIT ±1-2 for random shape
   123→- GEMM: Random log2_ks ±1 or kernel swap for random shape
   124→- MLA: Random splits ×2, ÷2, or ±4 for random shape
   125→
   126→## Kernel-Specific Search Spaces
   127→
   128→### MoE (7 benchmark shapes, gap: 1.27x)
   129→Primary lever: Per-shape KSPLIT lookup table. Values 0-6.
   130→Key shapes: E=257 (256 routed + 1 shared) and E=33 (32 routed + 1 shared).
   131→
   132→### GEMM (6 benchmark shapes, gap: 2.4x)
   133→Primary lever: Per-shape kernel selection (gemm_a4w4 vs gemm_a4w4_asm) + split-K (log2_ks 0-4).
   134→Key shapes: M=4 (bandwidth-bound) and M=256 (compute-bound).
   135→
   136→### MLA (8 benchmark shapes, gap: 15.6x)
   137→Primary lever: Adaptive num_kv_splits per (bs, kvseqlen). Also: FP8 vs MXFP4 KV format.
   138→Key shapes: bs=4/kv=1024 (few splits) to bs=128/kv=8192 (many splits).
   139→
   140→## Results Analysis
   141→
   142→```bash
   143→# View latest results
   144→tail -5 results/moe_runs.jsonl | uv run python -m json.tool
   145→
   146→# Find best result per kernel
   147→uv run python -c "
   148→from analyzer import get_best_result
   149→from pathlib import Path
   150→for k in ['moe', 'gemm', 'mla']:
   151→    best = get_best_result(Path(f'results/{k}_runs.jsonl'))
   152→    if best: print(f'{k}: {best[\"geomean_us\"]:.1f}µs')
   153→    else: print(f'{k}: no results yet')
   154→"
   155→
   156→# View tree stats
   157→uv run python -c "
   158→from ksearch_tree import KSearchTree
   159→from pathlib import Path
   160→for k in ['moe', 'gemm', 'mla']:
   161→    t = KSearchTree.load(Path(f'tree/{k}_tree.json'))
   162→    print(t)
   163→"
   164→```
   165→
   166→## Dead Ends (DO NOT RETRY)
   167→
   168→- `doweight_stage1=True` — 82% mismatch or GPU crash
   169→- `torch.compile(fused_moe)` — assertion crash on ROCm 7.1
   170→- Pure Triton kernels — 50-70% slower than CK/ASM
   171→- hiprtc compilation — blocked by runner
   172→- `expert_mask=bincount` — GPU memory fault
   173→- `num_kv_splits=64+` — exceeds aiter limits
   174→- `AITER_JIT_DIR` pre-caching — internal error 1
   175→
   176→## Coordination
   177→
   178→This system is registered in `COORDINATION.md` as the `autoresearch` session.
   179→It follows the staging directory protocol: backups are saved to `kernels/<kernel>/staging/`
   180→before overwriting `submission.py`. The rate limiter enforces 1 leaderboard submission
   181→per hour per problem to avoid API abuse.
   182→

1→# Research Module
     2→
     3→Elegant integration of autonomous research (karpathy/autoresearch) into Cohezion.
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→This module enables **autonomous AI-driven training optimization** using Cohezion's compound executor infrastructure.
     8→
     9→**Design Philosophy:** Single responsibility, plugin architecture, minimal code.
    10→
    11→## Architecture
    12→
    13→```
    14→src/cohezion/research/
    15→├── __init__.py          # Clean exports
    16→├── config.py            # ResearchConfig + ExperimentResult (~100 lines)
    17→└── agent.py            # ResearchAgent (~180 lines)
    18→
    19→Total: ~280 lines (vs autoresearch's ~500 lines standalone)
    20→```
    21→
    22→## Key Features
    23→
    24→**1. Leverages Existing Infrastructure**
    25→- Uses `CompoundExecutor` for experiment orchestration
    26→- Uses Cohezion's metrics/persistence systems
    27→- Uses existing security guardrails
    28→- Zero duplication
    29→
    30→**2. Plugin Architecture**
    31→```python
    32→# Optional integration - doesn't force usage
    33→from cohezion.research import ResearchAgent
    34→
    35→agent = ResearchAgent(
    36→    config=ResearchConfig(),
    37→    executor=existing_executor,  # Optional
    38→)
    39→```
    40→
    41→**3. Single Responsibility**
    42→- `ResearchAgent`: Run experiments
    43→- `ResearchConfig`: Configuration
    44→- `ResearchSession`: State tracking
    45→- Each class < 200 lines

## Complete Report: Autoresearch in Cohezion

### What is Autoresearch?

**Autoresearch** is an autonomous research system that runs unattended optimization loops to systematically explore solution spaces and improve performance metrics. It's inspired by [karpathy/autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch) but deeply integrated into Cohezion's compound engineering infrastructure.

Autoresearch operates at two complementary levels:

1. **Generic Level** (for training/ML optimization): `/src/cohezion/research/` - ~280 lines of elegant code wrapping experiment loops into the Cohezion compound executor
2. **Specialized Level** (for kernel optimization): `luma_speedrun/autoresearch/` - K-Search tree-based overnight kernel parameter optimization for AMD MI355X competition

---

### Core Components

#### 1. **AutoresearchExecutor** (`src/cohezion/swarm/autoresearch_executor.py`)

The base executor for hypothesis-driven research:

- **Core Loop**: Evaluate research hypotheses → measure execution speed and coherence → conditionally trigger R-Zero evolution
- **Key Features**:
  - Dynamic runtime bounds based on hardware speed (minimum 10 tokens/sec)
  - HIHO coherence gate at 0.5 threshold (triggers R-Zero evolver on high coherence)
  - Session management via `CompoundSessionManager` (caching, checkpoints)
  - Benchmarking of model inference speed for hardware-aware tuning

- **Use Cases**: Testing AGI boundary limitations, benchmark hypothesis evaluation, epistemic humility validation

#### 2. **ThermalAutoresearchExecutor** (`src/cohezion/compound/thermal_autoresearch_executor.py`)

Extended version with comprehensive thermal + power management:

- **Duration**: Supports 8-hour overnight runs
- **Protection Systems**:
  - Thermal checkpointing: Pauses at 90°C, resumes at 80°C
  - TDP budget tracking: 120W envelope for 8 hours
  - Ralph Loop coherence gates: HIHO threshold at 0.5
  - Cooldown cycles: 5-min pause every 60 min
  
- **Multi-Domain Sequential Execution**: 4 domains (GPU optimization, FLUME refinement, architecture analysis, synthesis)
- **Persistence**: SurrealDB journey tracking + Obsidian vault logging
- **Hardware-Aware**: Monitors GPU/CPU temps, scales intensity on thermal warnings

#### 3. **K-Search Driver** (`luma_speedrun/autoresearch/driver.py`)

Specialized for autonomous kernel optimization (competition context):

- **Tree-Structured Search**: Each kernel (GEMM, MoE, MLA) has a K-Search tree with ~11-14 nodes
- **Cycle Operations** (per node):
  1. **SELECT**: Pick highest-priority leaf node
  2. **SYNTHESIZE**: LLM-generated kernel parameters (or fallback to baseline)
  3. **TEST**: Correctness check via popcorn-cli
  4. **BENCHMARK**: Measure timing on 6-8 benchmark shapes
  5. **ANALYZE**: Update tree priorities, mark stagnant nodes
  6. **LEADERBOARD**: Submit if improved + rate-limited (1/hour)

- **Parameter Spaces**:
  - **MoE**: Per-shape KSPLIT lookup (0-6 values)
  - **GEMM**: Kernel selection + split-K (log2_ks 0-4)
  - **MLA**: Adaptive num_kv_splits per (batch, seq_len) + KV format choice

- **Cross-Kernel Learning**: Propagate failures/successes across GEMM, MoE, MLA trees

#### 4. **ResearchAgent** (`src/cohezion/research/agent.py`)

High-level training optimization agent:

- **Integration**: Plugs into `CompoundExecutor` for experiment orchestration
- **State**: Tracks session_id, experiments_completed, best_metric, best_checkpoint
- **Circuit Breaker**: Reliability protection (fails open after 5 consecutive failures)
- **Minimal Code**: ~200 lines (vs autoresearch's ~500 lines standalone)

---

### How Autoresearch Works

#### Generic Research Loop (thermal_autoresearch_executor.py)

```
8-Hour Journey
├── Domain 1 (2h): GPU Kernel Optimization
│   ├── Hypothesis: "Optimize MXFP4 GEMM for MI355X"
│   ├── Evaluation: LLM coherence scoring
│   ├── Ralph Loop Gate: Coherence >= 0.5 → passes
│   └── R-Zero Trigger: Coherence >= 0.8 → run evolver
├── Domain 2 (2h): FLUME Self-Improvement
│   ├── Hypothesis: "Refine VAE for 12D projection"
│   ├── Evaluation: Coherence scoring
│   └── Thermal Check: Pause if GPU > 90°C
├── Domain 3 (2h): Architecture Analysis
├── Domain 4 (2h): Cross-Domain Synthesis
└── Final Report: Journey completion stats, thermal events, TDP consumed
```

**Thermal Protection During Execution**:
- Pre-execution: Check temp, decide if safe to proceed
- During: Monitor TDP budget (120Wh for 8h)
- On threshold: Create checkpoint, cooldown 5min
- Resume: Load checkpoint, continue

#### K-Search Optimization Loop (driver.py - luma_speedrun)

```
Cycle (repeat ~75x overnight):
├── SELECT kernel: Priority-weighted (MoE 50%, GEMM 30%, MLA 20%)
├── SELECT node: Best unfinished node from kernel's tree
├── SYNTHESIZE: LLM generates kernel code with params
├── TEST: popcorn-cli correctness check
├── BENCHMARK: Get timing on 6-8 shapes → geomean
├── UPDATE: Adjust tree node priority, track stagnation
├── CROSS-KERNEL: Propagate success/failure to other trees
├── LEADERBOARD: Submit if new best (rate-limited 1/hr)
└── SLEEP: 5 seconds
```

**Rate Limiting**: Max 1 leaderboard submission per hour per problem (to avoid API abuse)

---

### Integration with Vault & Graph

#### Vault Integration:
1. **Journey Persistence** (`JourneyPersistence`): Saves 12D trajectory coordinates to vault
2. **Decision Logging**: `vault_log_decision()` captures research decisions
3. **Pattern Extraction**: `vault_extract_pattern()` for reusable kernel templates
4. **Experience Guidance**: Query vault for similar prior experiments before executing

#### SurrealDB Graph Integration:
1. **Journey Tracking**: Records execution states, coherence scores, thermal events
2. **Anomaly Detection**: Detects drift in coherence (triggers alerts)
3. **Cross-Domain Linking**: Connects insights from multiple domains
4. **Lineage**: Tracks which hypotheses led to which improvements

#### MCP Integration:
1. **Compound Client** (`get_compound_client()`): Interfaces with language models
2. **Hardware Monitor**: Real-time temp/power metrics
3. **Code Synthesis**: LLM-generated kernel code (via `synthesize_kernel()`)

---

### Key Design Patterns

| Pattern | Purpose | Example |
|---------|---------|---------|
| **HIHO Coherence Gate** | Filter low-quality hypotheses | Require coherence >= 0.5 before R-Zero |
| **Thermal Checkpointing** | Survive thermal events | Save state at 90°C, resume after cooldown |
| **TDP Budget Tracking** | Respect hardware envelope | Throttle if consuming >80% of 120Wh |
| **K-Search with Stagnation** | Auto-prune bad strategies | Mark as stagnant after 7 attempts, prune |
| **Cross-Kernel Propagation** | Share discoveries | If GEMM fails strategy X, close X in MoE too |
| **Rate Limiting** | Prevent API abuse | Max 1 leaderboard/hr/problem |
| **Circuit Breaker** | Reliability | Fail open after 5 consecutive errors |

---

### Files & Locations

**Core Autoresearch**:
- `/src/cohezion/swarm/autoresearch_executor.py` - Base hypothesis evaluator
- `/src/cohezion/compound/thermal_autoresearch_executor.py` - 8-hour thermal variant
- `/src/cohezion/research/agent.py` - Training optimization agent
- `/src/cohezion/research/README.md` - Module documentation

**K-Search Kernel Optimization**:
- `/luma_speedrun/autoresearch/driver.py` - Main overnight loop
- `/luma_speedrun/autoresearch/code_synthesizer.py` - LLM kernel generation
- `/luma_speedrun/autoresearch/popcorn.py` - Evaluation wrapper (test/benchmark/leaderboard)
- `/research/challenges/luma_amd_speedrun/autoresearch/` - Full implementation

**Configuration & Persistence**:
- `/src/cohezion/compound/thermal_checkpoint_manager.py` - Checkpoint/resume logic
- `/src/cohezion/compound/tdp_budget_tracker.py` - Power envelope tracking
- `/src/cohezion/compound/journey_tracker.py` - 12D trajectory recording

**Agents & Commands**:
- `/.claude/agents/tree-evolver.md` - K-Search evolution agent (runs cycles)
- `/.claude/commands/scout.md` - Market scout for model discovery
- `/.claude/agents/kernel-writer.md` - Kernel generation agent
- `/.claude/agents/kernel-researcher.md` - Kernel analysis agent

**Tests**:
- `/tests/swarm/test_autoresearch_executor.py` - Unit tests

---

### Quick Reference: Running Autoresearch

```bash
# Generic research (8-hour thermal journey)
uv run python scripts/drivers/run_8hr_journey.py

# K-Search kernel optimization (overnight)
cd luma_speedrun/autoresearch
python driver.py --max-cycles 50  # Full run

# Dry-run (validate templates, no popcorn-cli needed)
python driver.py --dry-run --max-cycles 5

# Single kernel sprint
python driver.py --kernel moe --max-cycles 20

# Tree evolver agent (CLI)
tree-evolver run --kernel gemm --model qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

---

### Summary

**Autoresearch** is Cohezion's system for autonomous, unattended optimization. It combines:

1. **Hypothesis-driven research** (coherence scoring, HIHO gates, R-Zero triggers)
2. **Thermal protection** (checkpointing, TDP budgeting, cooldown cycles)
3. **K-Search tree optimization** (systematic kernel parameter exploration)
4. **Vault integration** (persistence, pattern extraction, experience guidance)
5. **Graph observability** (journey tracking, anomaly detection, cross-domain linking)

The system is designed for long-duration runs (8+ hours) with hardware-aware safety constraints, integrated with Cohezion's compound executor, and extensively used for the AMD E2E Model Speedrun competition.

Based on my thorough search, here's what I found about Ralph Loop:

## Ralph Loop: Complete Summary

**Ralph Loop** is an official Anthropic Claude Code plugin (from the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace) that implements a **self-referential iterative development loop** within a single Claude session.

### What It Does

Ralph Loop creates an automated feedback cycle where:

1. **Initialization**: You provide a task prompt via `/ralph-loop "your task"` command
2. **State Management**: Creates a state file at `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` with metadata (iteration count, max iterations, completion promise, etc.)
3. **Infinite Iteration**: When you try to exit the session, the same prompt is fed back to you automatically
4. **Continuous Improvement**: You see your previous work in files and git history, allowing iterative refinement
5. **Completion Conditions**: Loop terminates only when:
   - Maximum iterations (if set via `--max-iterations N`) is reached, OR
   - A completion promise (set via `--completion-promise TEXT`) is output in the exact XML format

### Key Features

| Feature | Details |
|---------|---------|
| **Entry Point** | `/ralph-loop PROMPT [--max-iterations N] [--completion-promise TEXT]` |
| **State File** | `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` (YAML frontmatter + prompt) |

# Tree Evolver Agent

You run the K-Search autoresearch driver to evolve optimization trees via LLM world model.

## Setup Checklist
1. Ensure only ONE Ollama model is loaded (check: `curl -s http://localhost:11434/api/ps`)
2. Unload competing models: `ollama stop <model-name>`
3. Verify timeout in `code_synthesizer.py` is >= 1800 (30 min for CPU inference)

## Running Cycles
```bash
cd /home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/research/challenges/luma_amd_speedrun/autoresearch
python3 -u driver.py --dry-run-llm --max-cycles 1 --kernel <kernel> --model qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

CRITICAL: Run kernels SEQUENTIALLY, never in parallel. CPU memory bandwidth is shared.

## Expected Timing (CPU-only, Strix Halo)
- Model load (cold): ~60s
- Model load (warm): ~0s
- World model evolution: ~15-20 min per cycle
- Total per kernel: ~15-20 min

## Success Indicators
- "LLM INSERT" in output = new strategy proposed
- "LLM UPDATE" = priority adjusted
- "PRUNE" = dead branch removed
- Partial JSON parse error = timed out (increase OLLAMA_TIMEOUT)

## After Runs
1. Show tree state: `python3 -c "import json; ..."`
2. Commit trees: `git add tree/ && git commit -m "..."`
3. Mark task completed, SendMessage to team-lead

## Model Selection
- Default: `qwen2.5-coder:7b` (4.7GB, ~0.15 tok/s on CPU)
- Quality: `qwen3-coder:30b` (19.5GB, ~0.06 tok/s — overnight only)
- Fast: `gemma3:4b` (3.3GB, ~0.3 tok/s — lower quality)

import asyncio
import logging
import re
import time
from typing import Any

from cohezion.compound.session_manager import CompoundSessionManager
from cohezion.swarm.compound_client import get_compound_client
from cohezion.swarm.r_zero_evolver import RZeroEvolver


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class AutoresearchExecutor:
    """
    Executes an Autoresearch loop focused on Metacognition (Epistemic Humility).
    Uses dynamic runtime bounds based on model execution speed to optimize
    for the local 128GB RAM hardware profile.
    Incorporates KalshiBench and HumbleBench principles.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        min_speed_tokens_sec: float = 10.0,
        max_duration_seconds: int = 3600,
        r_zero_success_target: int = 5,
    ):
        self.min_speed_tokens_sec = min_speed_tokens_sec
        self.max_duration_seconds = max_duration_seconds
        self.r_zero_success_target = r_zero_success_target
        self.start_time = 0.0

    async def _evaluate_hypothesis(
        self, hypothesis: str, mgr: CompoundSessionManager
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Evaluate an autoresearch hypothesis for Epistemic Humility testing."""
        client = get_compound_client()

        prompt = (
            f"Evaluate the following benchmark hypothesis for testing Epistemic Humility:\n"
            f"{hypothesis}\n\n"
            f"Consider principles from:\n"
            f"1. KalshiBench (Extended Reasoning Overconfidence)\n"
            f"2. HumbleBench (False-Option Rejection / 'Insufficient Info')\n\n"
            f"Does this hypothesis advance our ability to measure AGI boundary limitations? "
            f"Provide a coherence score (0.0 to 1.0)."
        )

        t0 = time.time()
        # Use premium model for reasoning
        response_text, _ = await client.generate(
            prompt=prompt,
            model="gemini-3-pro:local",
            system="You are a senior AI research scientist evaluating benchmark proposals.",
        )
        t1 = time.time()

        # Simple speed metric
        duration = t1 - t0
        approx_tokens = len(response_text) / 4.0  # rough estimate
        tokens_per_sec = approx_tokens / duration if duration > 0 else 0.0

        coherence = 0.0
        # Parse coherence (heuristic)
        if (
            "coherence score" in response_text.lower()
            or "0." in response_text
            or "1.0" in response_text
        ):
            try:
                lines = response_text.split("\n")
                for line in lines:
                    match = re.search(r"0\.[0-9]+|1\.0", line)
                    if match:
                        coherence = float(match.group())
                        break
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to parse coherence: {e}")

options.description: Autoresearch cycles write discoveries (hypotheses, results, K-Search mutations) to the neuron graph as new neurons + synapses. Graph grows with each research cycle.

options.label: Ralph Loop graph annotations
options.description: Ralph Loop iterations annotate neurons with access patterns (which neurons were queried, how activation changed). Creates a live usage heatmap.

options.label: Both + scout integration
options.description: Full loop: Scout finds models → Autoresearch tests them → Results become neurons → Ralph Loop iterates → Graph reflects all activity. Scout command also writes findings to graph.

options.label: Something else
options.description: I have a different integration in mind

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Autonomous K-Search experiment driver.

Main overnight loop:
  SELECT node → generate submission → popcorn-cli test → benchmark
  → UPDATE tree → log JSONL → rotate kernels → repeat

Usage:
  uv run python driver.py                    # Run all kernels (priority-weighted)
  uv run python driver.py --kernel moe       # Run only MoE experiments
  uv run python driver.py --kernel gemm      # Run only GEMM experiments
  uv run python driver.py --kernel mla       # Run only MLA experiments
  uv run python driver.py --max-cycles 10    # Limit number of cycles
  uv run python driver.py --dry-run          # Generate submissions but don't submit
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import logging
import random
import shutil
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path


# Add autoresearch to path
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent))

import generator
from analyzer import Analysis, analyze_result, evolve_world_model, log_result
from code_synthesizer import is_ollama_available
from evaluator import KERNEL_DIRS, EvalResult, evaluate
from generator import generate_submission
from ksearch_tree import KSearchTree
from rate_limiter import RateLimiter


logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
    datefmt="%H:%M:%S",
)
log = logging.getLogger("autoresearch")

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent
TREE_DIR = BASE_DIR / "tree"
RESULTS_DIR = BASE_DIR / "results"
KERNELS_DIR = BASE_DIR.parent / "kernels"

# Priority weights for kernel rotation (higher = more likely to be selected)
# Based on gap-to-leader: MoE 1.27x (closeable), GEMM 2.4x, MLA 15.6x
KERNEL_WEIGHTS = {
    "moe": 0.5,  # Closest to leader — highest ROI
    "gemm": 0.3,  # Medium gap
    "mla": 0.2,  # Largest gap — moonshot
}

# Extend Graph with Ralph Loop + Autoresearch + Scout Integration

## Context

The graph was just populated (11 → 354 neurons, 23 → 2,265 synapses) but it's **static**. Three active systems generate discoveries that should flow into the graph but currently don't:

| System | What It Produces | Where It Goes Today | Where It Should Go |
|--------|-----------------|--------------------|--------------------|
| **Autoresearch** (K-Search driver) | Tree mutations, benchmark results, strategy evaluations | `tree/*.json` + `results/*.jsonl` | Graph neurons + synapses |
| **Ralph Loop** | Iterative refinements, completion states | `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` (ephemeral) | Neuron annotations (access counts, notes) |
| **Scout** | Model candidates, HF trending papers | Console output only | Graph neurons (research findings) |

**Goal**: Create a live feedback loop where research activity flows into the graph, making it grow smarter with each cycle.

---

## Implementation

### Step 1: Create `graph_writer.py` — shared graph write module

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/graph_writer.py`

A lightweight module that any system can import to write to the neuron graph. Wraps the SurrealDB HTTP API with the same conventions as `sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py`.

```python
# API surface:
async def upsert_neuron(neuron_id, title, path, cluster, aspect, tags, content) -> bool
async def create_synapse(from_id, to_id, link_type, reason) -> bool
async def annotate_neuron(neuron_id, agent_notes, increment_access=True) -> bool
async def batch_upsert_neurons(neurons: list[dict]) -> int
```

Key design:
- Uses `surreal-ns`/`surreal-db` headers (SurrealDB v2 format, port 8001)
- Computes activation/stage/word_count internally (same formulas as sync script)
- Non-blocking: all operations wrapped in try/except, never crashes the caller
- Idempotent: UPSERT semantics throughout

### Step 2: Hook autoresearch driver into graph

**File**: `research/challenges/luma_amd_speedrun/autoresearch/driver.py`

After each cycle's `analyze_result()`, call `graph_writer` to:

1. **UPSERT a neuron** for the K-Search tree node that was tested:
   - ID: `neuron:ksearch_{kernel}_{node_id}_md`
   - cluster: `"autoresearch"`
   - title: strategy name from the tree node
   - tags: `["autoresearch", kernel_name, "k-search"]`
   - content: strategy description + latest result (e.g. "118.11µs geomean")

2. **Create a synapse** from the tree node neuron to the parent node neuron:
   - link_type: `"k-search-child"`

3. **Create a synapse** to the kernel's root concept neuron (if it exists in cortex):
   - e.g. `neuron:ksearch_gemm_root_md` → `neuron:mxfp4_quantization_md`
   - link_type: `"researches"`

**When**: After the `log_result()` call in the main cycle loop (~line 120 of driver.py).

### Step 3: Hook Ralph Loop into graph annotations

**File**: Create `.claude/hooks/ralph-graph-annotate.sh`

A **PostToolUse: Read** hook that detects when Ralph Loop reads a source file, and annotates the corresponding neuron:
- Increment `access_count` on the neuron matching that file path
- Update `last_accessed` timestamp
- Append iteration number to `agent_notes`

This is lightweight — it only fires when `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` exists (Ralph Loop is active).

**Alternative** (simpler): Instead of a hook, modify the Ralph Loop stop hook to write a summary to graph at end of each iteration. The stop hook already runs `entire hooks claude-code stop` — we add a graph annotation call there.

**Recommended approach**: Add a `ralph-graph-sync.py` script that the stop hook calls. It reads Ralph Loop state (iteration count, prompt) and annotates recently-accessed neurons.

### Step 4: Hook scout into graph

**File**: Modify `.claude/commands/scout.md` to include graph writing steps.

After finding model candidates, the scout should:

1. **UPSERT a neuron** for each discovered model:
   - ID: `neuron:model_{slugified_name}_md`
   - cluster: `"scout"`
   - tags: `["model-candidate", "scout", license, parameter_count]`
   - content: model description + reasoning

2. **Create synapses** to related concept neurons:
   - e.g. `neuron:model_qwen3_coder_30b_md` → `neuron:agentic_ai_md`
   - link_type: `"candidate-for"`

**Implementation**: The scout command already outputs structured data. Add a final step that calls the MCP `graph_write_latent_synapse` and `graph_annotate_neuron` tools, or calls `graph_writer.py` directly.

### Step 5: Add "autoresearch" cluster to graph stats

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/vault_graph/reactor.py`

No code change needed — the stored function `fn::vault_stats()` already groups by `cluster_id`. New clusters (`autoresearch`, `scout`) will appear automatically once neurons are created in them.

---

## Critical Files

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/graph_writer.py` | **CREATE** — shared graph write API |
| `research/challenges/.../autoresearch/driver.py` | **EDIT** — add graph_writer calls after each cycle |
| `.claude/commands/scout.md` | **EDIT** — add graph writing steps |
| `.claude/hooks/ralph-graph-annotate.sh` | **CREATE** — Ralph Loop → graph annotation hook |

### Existing code to reuse
- `sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py` — HTTP query pattern, activation/stage computation
- `vault_graph/tools.py` — `graph_write_latent_synapse`, `graph_annotate_neuron` MCP tools
- `graphrag_helpers.py:slugify()` — ID generation

---

## Data Flow (After Integration)

```
Scout (daily)
  └→ UPSERT neuron:model_* (cluster=scout)
      └→ synapse → cortex neurons (candidate-for)

Autoresearch (overnight)
  └→ UPSERT neuron:ksearch_* (cluster=autoresearch)
      └→ synapse → parent K-Search nodes (k-search-child)
      └→ synapse → cortex concepts (researches)

Ralph Loop (per iteration)
  └→ ANNOTATE neurons accessed during iteration
      └→ increment access_count, update last_accessed
      └→ activation recalculates based on recency

Graph (continuous)
  └→ 354+ neurons growing with each research cycle
  └→ graph_search / graph_neighborhood / graph_hops reflect live state
  └→ reactor.py bridging scores update to show cross-domain discoveries
```

---

## Verification

1. **graph_writer.py**: Unit test — upsert a test neuron, verify it appears in `graph_search`
2. **Autoresearch**: Run `driver.py --dry-run --max-cycles 1 --kernel gemm`, verify `neuron:ksearch_gemm_*` appears in graph
3. **Scout**: Run `/scout`, verify `neuron:model_*` appears in graph
4. **Ralph Loop**: Start `/ralph-loop "test" --max-iterations 1`, verify neuron annotations updated
5. **Full graph**: `graph_stats` should show new clusters (autoresearch, scout) alongside cortex/cerebellum

# Unify Graph Architecture — Bridge neuron ↔ vault_memory

## Context

Cohezion has **two separate graph systems** in SurrealDB that don't talk to each other:

| System | Table | Records | Edges | Used By |
|--------|-------|---------|-------|---------|
| **Neuron graph** | `neuron` + `synapse` | 11 | 23 | MCP graph tools (`graph_neighborhood`, `graph_search`, `graph_hops`, `graph_bridges`, `graph_stats`) |
| **GraphRAG** | `vault_memory` + `informed_by` | 343 | 2,265 | `reimport_vault.py`, vector similarity search |

The MCP tools that agents use interactively query the `neuron` table (11 records). The 343 vault notes with embeddings and 2,265 edges sit in `vault_memory` — invisible to graph tools. The import pipeline (`reimport_vault.py` + `graphrag_import.py`) correctly imports cortex/cerebellum but writes to the wrong table.

**Root cause**: The vault was reorganized from `papers/`+`concepts/` to `cortex/`+`cerebellum/` (brain-region structure). The old `surrealdb_sync.py` import (writes to `neuron`) still looks for the old directories. The new `graphrag_import.py` (writes to `vault_memory`) handles the new structure but the MCP graph tools don't read from it.

**Goal**: Make the 343 vault notes queryable through the MCP graph tools by syncing `vault_memory` → `neuron` + `synapse`.

## Approach: Sync Script (vault_memory → neuron)

Rather than rewriting either import system, create a **bridge script** that reads from `vault_memory` and populates `neuron` + `synapse`. This preserves both systems and is non-destructive.

### Why not just update the stored functions?

The stored functions (`fn::context_search`, `fn::vault_stats`, etc.) query the `neuron` table with specific fields (`activation`, `stage`, `cluster_id`, `aspect`, `synapse_out`, `synapse_in`, `word_count`). Changing them to query `vault_memory` would require adding all those computed fields to `vault_memory` — effectively duplicating the neuron schema. A sync script is cleaner.

---

## Implementation

### Step 1: Create `sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py`

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/scripts/sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py`

This script:
1. Reads all `vault_memory` records
2. Derives `cluster_id` from the `path` field (cortex/ → "cortex", cerebellum/ → "cerebellum")
3. Computes neuron metadata (activation, stage, word_count, aspect)
4. UPSERTs into the `neuron` table with the correct ID format (`neuron:cortex_<slug>`)
5. Converts `informed_by` edges → `synapse` edges
6. Reports before/after counts

**Key mapping**:
```
vault_memory:agent_architecture  →  neuron:cortex_agent_architecture_md
  type="neuron"                      cluster_id="cortex"
  path="cortex/agent-architecture.md" aspect="knower" (cortex) / "thinker" (cerebellum)
  content=<truncated>                 word_count=<computed>
  embedding=[768 floats]              stage=<computed from word_count>
  tags=[...]                          activation=<computed from completion+recency>
```

**Neuron ID derivation** (must match existing convention in stored functions):
- Path: `cortex/agent-architecture.md` → ID: `neuron:cortex_agent_architecture_md`
- Rule: Replace `/` with `_`, replace `-` with `_`, keep `.md` suffix as `_md`

**Stage computation** (reuse reactor.py logic):
- word_count < 100 → "embryo"
- word_count < 400 → "growing"
- word_count >= 400 → "mature"

**Activation computation** (reuse reactor.py logic):
- completion = min(word_count/400, 1.0) × 0.5 + stage_score × 0.3 + tag_score × 0.2
- recency = exp(-0.05 × days_since_modified)
- activation = completion × 0.7 + recency × 0.3

### Step 2: Create synapse edges from informed_by

For each `informed_by` edge (source vault_memory → target vault_memory):
1. Map both IDs to neuron IDs
2. Create `synapse` edge with `link_type = 'explicit'`

### Step 3: Update `surrealdb_sync.py` directory paths

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/surrealdb_sync.py`

Update hardcoded paths:
- Line 378, 407: `"papers"` → `"cortex"`
- Line 557, 588: `"concepts"` → `"cerebellum"`
- Line 638: `["papers", "concepts", "patterns", "decisions"]` → `["cortex", "cerebellum", "patterns", "decisions"]`

This fixes the old import system for future use, even though the sync script is the primary path.

### Step 4: Update MCP tool descriptions

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/server.py`

Update `surrealdb_import_papers` and `surrealdb_import_concepts` tool descriptions to reference cortex/cerebellum.

---

## Critical Files

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `cloud-vault-mcp/scripts/sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py` | **CREATE** — bridge script |
| `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/surrealdb_sync.py` | **EDIT** — update hardcoded directory paths (lines 378, 407, 557, 588, 638) |
| `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/server.py` | **EDIT** — update tool descriptions |
| `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/vault_graph/reactor.py` | **READ** — reuse activation/stage logic |

### Existing code to reuse

- `graphrag_import.py:slugify()` — ID generation
- `graphrag_helpers.py:parse_frontmatter()` — frontmatter extraction
- `vault_graph/reactor.py` — activation, stage, completion score computation
- `vault_graph/client.py` — SurrealDB HTTP client (port 8001, surreal-ns/surreal-db headers)

---

## Verification

1. **Run sync script**: `cd cloud-vault-mcp && uv run python scripts/sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py`
2. **Check neuron count**: Should go from 11 → 350+
3. **Check synapse count**: Should go from 23 → 2000+
4. **Test MCP graph tools**:
   - `graph_stats` → should show 350+ neurons
   - `graph_search("agent architecture")` → should find cortex notes
   - `graph_neighborhood("neuron:cortex_agent_architecture_md")` → should return neighbors
5. **Verify stage distribution**: Should show mix of embryo/growing/mature
6. **Verify cluster distribution**: Should show cortex (~257) and cerebellum (~95) clusters

| **Ralph Loop** | Iterative refinements, completion states | `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` (ephemeral) | Neuron annotations (access counts, notes) |
| **Scout** | Model candidates, HF trending papers | Console output only | Graph neurons (research findings) |

**Goal**: Create a live feedback loop where research activity flows into the graph, making it grow smarter with each cycle.

---

## Implementation

### Step 1: Create `graph_writer.py` — shared graph write module

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/graph_writer.py`

A lightweight module that any system can import to write to the neuron graph. Wraps the SurrealDB HTTP API with the same conventions as `sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py`.

```python
# API surface:
async def upsert_neuron(neuron_id, title, path, cluster, aspect, tags, content) -> bool
async def create_synapse(from_id, to_id, link_type, reason) -> bool
async def annotate_neuron(neuron_id, agent_notes, increment_access=True) -> bool
async def batch_upsert_neurons(neurons: list[dict]) -> int
```

Key design:
- Uses `surreal-ns`/`surreal-db` headers (SurrealDB v2 format, port 8001)
- Computes activation/stage/word_count internally (same formulas as sync script)
- Non-blocking: all operations wrapped in try/except, never crashes the caller
- Idempotent: UPSERT semantics throughout

### Step 2: Hook autoresearch driver into graph

**File**: `research/challenges/luma_amd_speedrun/autoresearch/driver.py`

After each cycle's `analyze_result()`, call `graph_writer` to:

1. **UPSERT a neuron** for the K-Search tree node that was tested:
   - ID: `neuron:ksearch_{kernel}_{node_id}_md`
   - cluster: `"autoresearch"`
   - title: strategy name from the tree node
   - tags: `["autoresearch", kernel_name, "k-search"]`
   - content: strategy description + latest result (e.g. "118.11µs geomean")

2. **Create a synapse** from the tree node neuron to the parent node neuron:
   - link_type: `"k-search-child"`

3. **Create a synapse** to the kernel's root concept neuron (if it exists in cortex):
   - e.g. `neuron:ksearch_gemm_root_md` → `neuron:mxfp4_quantization_md`
   - link_type: `"researches"`

**When**: After the `log_result()` call in the main cycle loop (~line 120 of driver.py).

### Step 3: Hook Ralph Loop into graph annotations

**File**: Create `.claude/hooks/ralph-graph-annotate.sh`

A **PostToolUse: Read** hook that detects when Ralph Loop reads a source file, and annotates the corresponding neuron:
- Increment `access_count` on the neuron matching that file path
- Update `last_accessed` timestamp
- Append iteration number to `agent_notes`

This is lightweight — it only fires when `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` exists (Ralph Loop is active).

**Alternative** (simpler): Instead of a hook, modify the Ralph Loop stop hook to write a summary to graph at end of each iteration. The stop hook already runs `entire hooks claude-code stop` — we add a graph annotation call there.

**File**: Modify `.claude/commands/scout.md` to include graph writing steps.

After finding model candidates, the scout should:

1. **UPSERT a neuron** for each discovered model:
   - ID: `neuron:model_{slugified_name}_md`
   - cluster: `"scout"`
   - tags: `["model-candidate", "scout", license, parameter_count]`
   - content: model description + reasoning

   - e.g. `neuron:model_qwen3_coder_30b_md` → `neuron:agentic_ai_md`
   - link_type: `"candidate-for"`

**Implementation**: The scout command already outputs structured data. Add a final step that calls the MCP `graph_write_latent_synapse` and `graph_annotate_neuron` tools, or calls `graph_writer.py` directly.

### Step 5: Add "autoresearch" cluster to graph stats

**File**: `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/vault_graph/reactor.py`

No code change needed — the stored function `fn::vault_stats()` already groups by `cluster_id`. New clusters (`autoresearch`, `scout`) will appear automatically once neurons are created in them.

---

## Critical Files

| File | Action |
|------|--------|
| `cloud-vault-mcp/src/mcp_server/graph_writer.py` | **CREATE** — shared graph write API |
| `research/challenges/.../autoresearch/driver.py` | **EDIT** — add graph_writer calls after each cycle |
| `.claude/commands/scout.md` | **EDIT** — add graph writing steps |
| `.claude/hooks/ralph-graph-annotate.sh` | **CREATE** — Ralph Loop → graph annotation hook |

### Existing code to reuse
- `sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py` — HTTP query pattern, activation/stage computation
- `vault_graph/tools.py` — `graph_write_latent_synapse`, `graph_annotate_neuron` MCP tools
- `graphrag_helpers.py:slugify()` — ID generation

---

## Data Flow (After Integration)

```
Scout (daily)
  └→ UPSERT neuron:model_* (cluster=scout)
      └→ synapse → cortex neurons (candidate-for)

Autoresearch (overnight)
  └→ UPSERT neuron:ksearch_* (cluster=autoresearch)

      └→ synapse → cortex concepts (researches)

Ralph Loop (per iteration)
  └→ ANNOTATE neurons accessed during iteration
      └→ increment access_count, update last_accessed

Graph (continuous)

"""Shared graph write API for neuron + synapse operations.

Used by autoresearch, Ralph Loop, scout, and any system that needs to
write discoveries back to the neuron graph in SurrealDB.

All operations are non-blocking (try/except), idempotent (UPSERT), and
use the same activation/stage formulas as sync_graphrag_to_neurons.py.
"""

import logging
import math
import os
import re
from datetime import date
from typing import Any

import httpx

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

SURREALDB_URL = os.environ.get("SURREALDB_URL", "http://localhost:8001")
NAMESPACE = os.environ.get("SURREALDB_NAMESPACE", "cohezion")
DATABASE = os.environ.get("SURREALDB_DATABASE", "vault")
AUTH = (
    os.environ.get("SURREALDB_USERNAME", "root"),
    os.environ.get("SURREALDB_PASSWORD", "root"),
)

LAMBDA_DECAY = 0.05


# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


def slugify(text: str) -> str:
    """Convert text to valid SurrealDB ID component."""
    slug = re.sub(r"[^\w\s-]", "", text.lower())
    slug = re.sub(r"[\s-]+", "_", slug)
    return slug.strip("_")


def escape_sql(text: str) -> str:
    """Escape for SurrealQL string literals."""
    return text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("'", "\\'")[:2000]


def compute_stage(word_count: int) -> str:
    if word_count < 100:
        return "embryo"
    elif word_count < 400:
        return "growing"
    return "mature"


def compute_activation(word_count: int, stage: str, tags: list, created_at: str = "") -> float:
    """Composite activation score matching reactor.py."""
    stage_scores = {"embryo": 0.1, "seedling": 0.3, "growing": 0.6, "mature": 1.0}
    stage_score = stage_scores.get(stage, 0.2)
    word_score = min(word_count / 400.0, 1.0)
    tag_score = min(len(tags) / 4.0, 1.0)
    completion = 0.5 * word_score + 0.3 * stage_score + 0.2 * tag_score

    recency = 0.0
    if created_at:
        try:
            d = date.fromisoformat(str(created_at)[:10])
            days = (date.today() - d).days
            recency = math.exp(-LAMBDA_DECAY * max(days, 0))
        except (ValueError, TypeError):
            pass

    return round(0.7 * completion + 0.3 * recency, 4)


# ── SurrealDB HTTP ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


async def _query(client: httpx.AsyncClient, sql: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Execute SurrealQL, return results."""
    resp = await client.post(
        f"{SURREALDB_URL}/sql",
        headers={
            "Content-Type": "text/plain",
            "Accept": "application/json",
            "surreal-ns": NAMESPACE,
            "surreal-db": DATABASE,
        },
        auth=AUTH,
        content=sql,
        timeout=10.0,
    )
    resp.raise_for_status()
    return resp.json()


# ── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────


async def upsert_neuron(
    neuron_id: str,
    title: str,
    path: str = "",
    cluster: str = "",
    aspect: str = "connective",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    content: str = "",
) -> bool:
    """Upsert a neuron with computed activation and stage.

    Args:
        neuron_id: Full SurrealDB ID (e.g. "neuron:ksearch_gemm_root_md")
        title: Display title
        path: Vault-relative path (optional)
        cluster: Cluster ID (cortex, cerebellum, autoresearch, scout, etc.)
        aspect: knower | thinker | connective
        tags: List of tag strings
        content: Text content for word count computation

    Returns:
        True if successful
    """
    tags = tags or []
    word_count = len(content.split()) if content else 0
    stage = compute_stage(word_count)
    activation = compute_activation(word_count, stage, tags, date.today().isoformat())

    sql = f"""UPSERT {neuron_id} SET
        title = '{escape_sql(title)}',
        path = '{escape_sql(path)}',
        cluster_id = '{escape_sql(cluster)}',
        aspect = '{escape_sql(aspect)}',
        stage = '{stage}',
        word_count = {word_count},
        activation = {activation},
        dim_completion = {round(min(word_count / 400.0, 1.0) * 0.5 + {"embryo": 0.1, "seedling": 0.3, "growing": 0.6, "mature": 1.0}.get(stage, 0.2) * 0.3 + min(len(tags) / 4.0, 1.0) * 0.2, 4)},
        dim_recency = 0.0,
        dim_bridging = 0.0,
        tags = {tags},
        synapse_in = 0,
        synapse_out = 0,
        modified = time::now(),
        last_fired = time::now();"""

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            ok = any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
            if ok:
                logger.info(f"Upserted {neuron_id} (cluster={cluster})")
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Upsert may have failed for {neuron_id}: {results}")
            return ok
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.upsert_neuron failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def create_synapse(
    from_id: str,
    to_id: str,
    link_type: str = "explicit",
    reason: str = "",
) -> bool:
    """Create a synapse edge between two neurons.

    Args:
        from_id: Source neuron ID
        to_id: Target neuron ID
        link_type: explicit | latent | dream | k-search-child | researches | candidate-for
        reason: Human-readable reason for the connection
    """
    reason_esc = escape_sql(reason)
    sql = f"""RELATE {from_id}->synapse->{to_id} SET
        link_type = '{escape_sql(link_type)}',
        reason = '{reason_esc}',
        created = time::now();"""

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            ok = any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
            if ok:
                logger.info(f"Synapse: {from_id} →[{link_type}]→ {to_id}")
            return ok
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.create_synapse failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def annotate_neuron(
    neuron_id: str,
    agent_notes: str = "",
    increment_access: bool = True,
) -> bool:
    """Annotate a neuron with metadata (does not touch structural fields).

    Args:
        neuron_id: Target neuron ID
        agent_notes: Free-form notes to append
        increment_access: Whether to increment access_count by 1
    """
    parts = [f"last_accessed = '{date.today().isoformat()}'"]
    if agent_notes:
        parts.append(f"agent_notes = '{escape_sql(agent_notes)}'")
    if increment_access:
        parts.append("access_count = (access_count ?? 0) + 1")

    sql = f"UPDATE {neuron_id} SET {', '.join(parts)};"

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            return any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.annotate_neuron failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def batch_upsert_neurons(neurons: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """Batch upsert multiple neurons.

    Each dict should have: neuron_id, title, and optionally:
    path, cluster, aspect, tags, content.

    Returns count of successfully upserted neurons.
    """
    if not neurons:
        return 0

    statements = []
    for n in neurons:
        tags = n.get("tags", [])
        content = n.get("content", "")
        word_count = len(content.split()) if content else 0
        stage = compute_stage(word_count)
        activation = compute_activation(word_count, stage, tags, date.today().isoformat())

        stmt = f"""UPSERT {n['neuron_id']} SET
            title = '{escape_sql(n["title"])}',
            path = '{escape_sql(n.get("path", ""))}',
            cluster_id = '{escape_sql(n.get("cluster", ""))}',
            aspect = '{escape_sql(n.get("aspect", "connective"))}',
            stage = '{stage}',
            word_count = {word_count},
            activation = {activation},
            tags = {tags},
            modified = time::now(),
            last_fired = time::now();"""
        statements.append(stmt)

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
            sql = "\n".join(statements)
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            count = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("status") == "OK")
            logger.info(f"Batch upserted {count}/{len(neurons)} neurons")
            return count
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.batch_upsert_neurons failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return 0

            ok = any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
            if ok:
                logger.info(f"Upserted {neuron_id} (cluster={cluster})")
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Upsert may have failed for {neuron_id}: {results}")
            return ok
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.upsert_neuron failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def create_synapse(
    from_id: str,
    to_id: str,
    link_type: str = "explicit",
    reason: str = "",
) -> bool:
    """Create a synapse edge between two neurons.

    Args:
        from_id: Source neuron ID
        to_id: Target neuron ID
        link_type: explicit | latent | dream | k-search-child | researches | candidate-for
        reason: Human-readable reason for the connection
    """
    reason_esc = escape_sql(reason)
    sql = f"""RELATE {from_id}->synapse->{to_id} SET
        link_type = '{escape_sql(link_type)}',
        reason = '{reason_esc}',
        created = time::now();"""

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            ok = any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
            if ok:
                logger.info(f"Synapse: {from_id} →[{link_type}]→ {to_id}")
            return ok
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.create_synapse failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def annotate_neuron(
    neuron_id: str,
    agent_notes: str = "",
    increment_access: bool = True,
) -> bool:
    """Annotate a neuron with metadata (does not touch structural fields).

    Args:
        neuron_id: Target neuron ID
        agent_notes: Free-form notes to append
        increment_access: Whether to increment access_count by 1
    """
    parts = [f"last_accessed = '{date.today().isoformat()}'"]
    if agent_notes:
        parts.append(f"agent_notes = '{escape_sql(agent_notes)}'")
    if increment_access:
        parts.append("access_count = (access_count ?? 0) + 1")

    sql = f"UPDATE {neuron_id} SET {', '.join(parts)};"

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=10.0) as client:
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            return any(r.get("status") == "OK" for r in results)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.annotate_neuron failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return False


async def batch_upsert_neurons(neurons: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
    """Batch upsert multiple neurons.

    Each dict should have: neuron_id, title, and optionally:
    path, cluster, aspect, tags, content.

    Returns count of successfully upserted neurons.
    """
    if not neurons:
        return 0

    statements = []
    for n in neurons:
        tags = n.get("tags", [])
        content = n.get("content", "")
        word_count = len(content.split()) if content else 0
        stage = compute_stage(word_count)
        activation = compute_activation(word_count, stage, tags, date.today().isoformat())

        stmt = f"""UPSERT {n['neuron_id']} SET
            title = '{escape_sql(n["title"])}',
            path = '{escape_sql(n.get("path", ""))}',
            cluster_id = '{escape_sql(n.get("cluster", ""))}',
            aspect = '{escape_sql(n.get("aspect", "connective"))}',
            stage = '{stage}',
            word_count = {word_count},
            activation = {activation},
            tags = {tags},
            modified = time::now(),
            last_fired = time::now();"""
        statements.append(stmt)

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30.0) as client:
            sql = "\n".join(statements)
            results = await _query(client, sql)
            count = sum(1 for r in results if r.get("status") == "OK")
            logger.info(f"Batch upserted {count}/{len(neurons)} neurons")
            return count
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"graph_writer.batch_upsert_neurons failed (non-blocking): {e}")
        return 0

CYCLE_SLEEP_SECONDS = 5  # Sleep between cycles


def load_tree(kernel: str) -> KSearchTree:
    """Load or create K-Search tree for a kernel."""
    tree_path = TREE_DIR / f"{kernel}_tree.json"
    if tree_path.exists():
        return KSearchTree.load(tree_path)
    tree = KSearchTree(kernel)
    tree.insert_root(f"Optimize {kernel} geomean")
    return tree


def save_tree(tree: KSearchTree) -> None:
    """Persist tree to disk."""
    tree_path = TREE_DIR / f"{tree.kernel_name}_tree.json"
    tree.save(tree_path)


def select_kernel(kernels: list[str]) -> str:
    """Weighted random selection of next kernel to optimize."""
    if len(kernels) == 1:
        return kernels[0]
    weights = [KERNEL_WEIGHTS.get(k, 0.33) for k in kernels]
    total = sum(weights)
    weights = [w / total for w in weights]
    return random.choices(kernels, weights=weights, k=1)[0]


def generate_variant_params(tree: KSearchTree, node) -> dict:
    """Generate a parameter variant from the node.

    If the node has been attempted before, slightly perturb parameters
    to explore nearby configurations.
    """
    params = dict(node.parameters)

    if node.attempts == 0:
        return params  # First attempt uses exact parameters

    # Perturbation: modify one random value in a lookup table
    kernel = tree.kernel_name

    if kernel == "moe" and "KSPLIT_TABLE" in params:
        table = dict(params["KSPLIT_TABLE"])
        if table:
            key = random.choice(list(table.keys()))
            current = table[key]
            # Perturb KSPLIT by ±1-2, clamped to 0-6
            delta = random.choice([-2, -1, 1, 2])
            table[key] = max(0, min(6, current + delta))
            params["KSPLIT_TABLE"] = table

    elif kernel == "gemm" and "KERNEL_TABLE" in params:
        table = dict(params["KERNEL_TABLE"])
        if table:
            key = random.choice(list(table.keys()))
            entry = dict(table[key])
            # Perturb log2_ks by ±1, clamped to 0-4
            delta = random.choice([-1, 1])
            entry["log2_ks"] = max(0, min(4, entry["log2_ks"] + delta))
            # Occasionally try ASM variant
            if random.random() < 0.3:
                entry["kernel"] = random.choice(["gemm_a4w4", "gemm_a4w4_asm"])
            table[key] = entry
            params["KERNEL_TABLE"] = table

    elif kernel == "mla" and "SPLITS_TABLE" in params:
        table = dict(params["SPLITS_TABLE"])
        if table:
            key = random.choice(list(table.keys()))
            current = table[key]
            # Perturb splits: ×2, ÷2, ±4
            choices = [
                max(2, current // 2),
                min(64, current * 2),
                max(2, current - 4),
                min(64, current + 4),
            ]
            table[key] = random.choice(choices)
            params["SPLITS_TABLE"] = table

    return params


def challenge_plateau(tree: KSearchTree, kernel: str, current_best: float) -> None:
    """R-Zero: Propose harder target when plateau detected.

    Instead of stopping at convergence, raise the bar by 10% and insert
    a new child node that targets the harder threshold.
    """
    new_target = current_best * 0.9  # 10% harder
    root_id = tree.root_id
    if not root_id:
        return

    # Check if we already have a challenger node for this level
    for node in tree.nodes.values():
        if f"Beat {new_target:.1f}µs" in node.strategy:
            return  # Already proposed this target

    tree.insert_child(
        parent_id=root_id,
        strategy=f"Beat {new_target:.1f}µs (10% below {current_best:.1f}µs plateau)",
        parameters={},
        priority=0.8,
        notes="[R-Zero challenger]",
    )
    log.info(
        f"[{kernel}] R-Zero: Raised target to {new_target:.1f}µs "
        f"(10% below plateau at {current_best:.1f}µs)"
    )

def run_cycle(
    kernel: str,
    tree: KSearchTree,
    rate_limiter: RateLimiter,
    dry_run: bool | str = False,
) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    """Run one experiment cycle for a kernel.

    Returns (success, summary_message).
    """
    # Select best node
    node = tree.select_best()
    if node is None:
        return False, f"{kernel}: No active nodes remaining"

    log.info(
        f"[{kernel}] Selected: {node.strategy} (p={node.priority:.2f}, attempts={node.attempts})"
    )

    # Generate variant parameters
    params = generate_variant_params(tree, node)

    # Get trajectory for LLM context
    trajectory = tree.get_trajectory(node.id)

    # Generate submission (skip LLM code synthesis in dry-run-llm to save time)
    template_key = params.pop("_template", kernel)
    use_llm_code = dry_run != "llm"  # dry-run-llm focuses on world model, not code gen
    try:
        code = generate_submission(
            template_key,
            params,
            strategy=node.strategy,
            trajectory=trajectory,
            use_llm=use_llm_code,
        )
    except ValueError as e:
        log.error(f"[{kernel}] Generation failed: {e}")
        tree.mark_failed(node.id, str(e))
        save_tree(tree)
        return False, f"{kernel}: Generation failed: {e}"

    if dry_run == "llm":
        # Dry-run with LLM: skip code synthesis, focus on world model evolution
        log.info(f"[{kernel}] DRY RUN (LLM) — {len(code)} chars (template), testing world model...")
        synthetic_geomean = (node.best_result_us or 200.0) * random.uniform(0.85, 1.15)
        synthetic_result = EvalResult(
            kernel=kernel,
            mode="benchmark",
            success=True,
            geomean_us=round(synthetic_geomean, 2),
        )
        analysis = analyze_result(synthetic_result, tree, node)
        node.record_attempt(
            result_us=synthetic_geomean,
            parameters=params,
            source=generator.last_source,
        )
        try:
            counts = evolve_world_model(tree, node, synthetic_result, analysis)
            log.info(f"[{kernel}] World model: {counts}")
        except Exception as e:
            log.warning(f"[{kernel}] World model evolution failed: {e}")
        save_tree(tree)
        return True, (
            f"{kernel}: Dry run LLM OK "
            f"(synthetic={synthetic_geomean:.1f}µs, "
            f"source={generator.last_source}, "
            f"{len(tree.nodes)} nodes)"
        )
    elif dry_run:
        log.info(f"[{kernel}] DRY RUN — would submit {len(code)} chars")
        return True, f"{kernel}: Dry run OK ({len(code)} chars)"

    # Write submission to kernel directory
    kernel_dir = KERNELS_DIR / KERNEL_DIRS[kernel]
    staging_dir = kernel_dir / "staging"
    staging_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Save to staging with timestamp
    ts = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    staged_path = staging_dir / f"submission.autoresearch.{ts}.py"
    staged_path.write_text(code)

    # Copy to submission.py for popcorn-cli
    submission_path = kernel_dir / "submission.py"
    # Back up current submission
    backup_path = staging_dir / f"submission.backup.{ts}.py"
    if submission_path.exists():
        shutil.copy2(submission_path, backup_path)
    submission_path.write_text(code)

    # Test first, then benchmark
    log.info(f"[{kernel}] Testing...")
    test_result = evaluate(submission_path, kernel, mode="test")

    if not test_result.success:
        log.warning(f"[{kernel}] Test FAILED: {test_result.error}")
        tree.mark_failed(node.id, f"Test failed: {test_result.error}")
        # Restore backup
        if backup_path.exists():
            shutil.copy2(backup_path, submission_path)
        save_tree(tree)
        # Log failure
        log_result(
            test_result,
            node,
            Analysis(float("inf"), None, 0.0, {}, test_result.error),
            RESULTS_DIR / f"{kernel}_runs.jsonl",
        )
        return False, f"{kernel}: Test failed: {test_result.error}"

    log.info(f"[{kernel}] Test PASSED. Benchmarking...")
    bench_result = evaluate(submission_path, kernel, mode="benchmark")

    if not bench_result.success:
        log.warning(f"[{kernel}] Benchmark FAILED: {bench_result.error}")
        # Still update tree (test passed, benchmark failed is different from correctness failure)
        if backup_path.exists():
            shutil.copy2(backup_path, submission_path)
